description: “I coded a Rover Mission Game where the rover races through a maze to save the astronaut on the Moon!” – Adwaith Arun, Grade 4C
summary: “I coded a Rover Mission Game where the rover races through a maze to save the astronaut on the Moon!” – Adwaith Arun, Grade 4C
details:
My game is a space rescue mission. An astronaut on the Moon needs water, oxygen, food and exercise equipment to survive. The player steers a rover through a maze to collect them. A timer is running, and the rover must reach the oxygen within 10 seconds. If the rover touches a maze wall, the mission fails and the player tries again.

What benefits does it have?
It helps players practise quick thinking, planning and hand–eye coordination. It also teaches what astronauts need to survive in space.

What is the intended impact?
I want children to get curious about space and coding, and to see that failing is part of learning. You just try again.

What tools did you use?
I used Scratch (block-based coding) on a laptop. I coded sprites, a timer variable, sensing blocks to detect walls and items, and conditions for winning and losing.

How is it creative?
I turned a real space problem into a fun game. I designed the maze on a lunar background, used real astronaut needs as items to collect, and added a time challenge to make it exciting.

What factors did I consider?

  • Difficulty: The game had to be easy to understand and still challenging.
  • Fair timing: 10 seconds to reach the oxygen.
  • Clear rules: Walls end the mission.
  • Feedback: Players see clear messages when they win or fail.
